title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection thresholds and rollout guards with hysteresis
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Enhances performance canary auto-detection accuracy and adds hysteresis-backed rollout guards to reduce flapping during transient noise. Backwards compatible with existing canary configs.
description: Context: our continuous performance canary pipeline has been producing false positives during transient infra noise and bursty traffic patterns, which caused unnecessary rollbacks and manual interventions. This PR updates the canary detector and rollout guard logic to add dynamic threshold estimation and hysteresis so that small transient regressions do not trigger immediate rollbacks and we have clearer signals for true regressions. Changes include: 1) dynamic baseline calculation using an exponentially-weighted moving percentiles (EWMP) estimator for latency and throughput metrics; 2) hysteresis window for rollout guards (separate detect/resolve thresholds and a stabilization timeout) to avoid flapping when metrics hover around thresholds; 3) per-model weighting and traffic-aware thresholds so that low-traffic routes have higher statistical tolerance; 4) improved telemetry and dashboards (new Grafana panels and alert labels) to surface confidence and sample sizes; 5) unit and integration tests + canary test harness improvements to reproduce noisy scenarios. Motivation: reduce operational churn from spurious canary failures while preserving sensitivity to meaningful regressions. Related: ENG-1428 (canary false-positive reduction), ENG-1502 (rollout guard improvements). Implementation notes: detector now computes the 95th/50th EWMP over a rolling 30m window and falls back to historical percentiles when sample count < min_samples. The rollout guard uses separate enter_threshold and exit_threshold values with a default hysteresis factor of 1.15 and a stabilization timeout of 5 minutes. We added a new config block `detection.hysteresis` and `detection.dynamic_baseline` that are opt-in for existing canaries; default behavior is backward-compatible. Observability: emits canary.confidence, canary.sample_count, and canary.baseline_percentile metrics. Tests: added deterministic unit tests for EWMP, integration test that simulates noisy traffic and verifies no rollback within stabilization timeout, e2e smoke test that exercises the Grafana panels. Rollout: merged to main after approval; feature is toggleable by canary config to allow safe rollout across clusters.

changes_summary: Adds EWMP-based dynamic baseline, hysteresis-backed rollout guard with enter/exit thresholds and stabilization timeout, per-route sample-aware thresholds, new metrics, tests and dashboard updates. Config is opt-in with backward-compatible defaults.
ci_checks: ci/integration (canary_integration): passed (7m12s) after one rerun due to infra flake
review_conversation: Ben Torres: Can you clarify the default hysteresis factor and whether it's configurable?
Aisha Khan: Default is 1.15 for hysteresis factor and it's configurable under detection.hysteresis.factor. Added notes in docs and validated in unit tests.
Claire Li: The EWMP estimator looks good but ensure it degrades gracefully on low-sample routes.Suggested fallback to historical percentiles.
Aisha Khan: Implemented fallback to historical percentiles when sample_count < detection.dynamic_baseline.min_samples (default 50). Added integration test to validate behavior.
Marcus Jensen: Integration run showed one flake due to CI infra, reran and green. Approving after test coverage is confirmed.
notes_for_ops: New canary configs added under detection.dynamic_baseline and detection.hysteresis. Defaults maintain old behavior but ops can opt-in per-route. Watch canary.confidence and canary.sample_count metrics for first 24h post-rollout. Grafana dashboard and alert labels updated: 'Canary - Confidence' and 'Canary - Sample Size'.
backfill_instructions: No immediate backfill required. To enable dynamic baseline for existing canaries, set detection.dynamic_baseline.enabled: true and optionally tune min_samples and hysteresis.factor. For low-traffic routes increase min_samples to avoid frequent fallbacks.
risk_assessment: Low: feature is opt-in and backward-compatible. Risk originates from misconfiguration causing reduced sensitivity; mitigated by sane defaults and monitoring metrics. Added temporary alert to notify if sample_count consistently < min_samples.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for EWMP and hysteresis logic. Integration test simulates bursty traffic and validates stabilization timeout prevents rollback. E2E smoke test verifies dashboard wiring. CI showed one transient failure that was rerun and resolved.
notes: This PR addresses long-standing noise in canary detection and should significantly reduce false-positive rollbacks. Ops and SRE should monitor for sample_count and baseline shifts during the first week after enabling on any critical routes.
